# Problem 1
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(p8105.datasets)
library(tidyverse)

data("ny_noaa")

ny_noaa
```
We want to know the size and the structure of the data.
## Overview of the data
```{r}
dim(ny_noaa)
glimpse(ny_noaa)
summary(ny_noaa)

ny_noaa |>
  summarise(
    total_rows = n(),
    total_stations = n_distinct(id),
    missing_date = sum(is.na(date)),
    missing_prcp = sum(is.na(prcp)),
    missing_snow = sum(is.na(snow)),
    missing_snwd = sum(is.na(snwd)),
    missing_tmax = sum(is.na(tmax)),
    missing_tmin = sum(is.na(tmin))
  )
```
A short description based on the data:
The `ny_noaa` dataset contains daily weather observations from `r scales::comma(nrow(ny_noaa))` records across `r n_distinct(ny_noaa$id)` weather stations in New York State. It has `r ncol(ny_noaa)` variables, including station ID (`id`), observation date (`date`), precipitation (`prcp`), snowfall (`snow`), snow depth (`snwd`), maximum temperature (`tmax`), and minimum temperature (`tmin`). The observations span from 1981 to 2010. Missing data are an important issue. Precipitation has 145,838 missing values, snowfall has 381,221, and snow depth has 591,786. The temperature variables (tmax and tmin) are stored as character variables, and their missing values should also be examined.

## Data Cleaning
```{r}
noaa_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(str_sub(date, 1, 4)),
    month = as.numeric(str_sub(date, 6, 7)),
    day = as.numeric(str_sub(date, 9, 10)),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = as.numeric(prcp) / 10,
    snow = as.numeric(snow),
    snwd = as.numeric(snwd)
  )
```

Snow falls
```{r}
noaa_df |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)
```
The most commonly observed snowfall value is expected to be 0 mm because snowfall does not occur on most observation days. 

## Average max temperature in January and in July
```{r, warning=FALSE}
temp_df =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarise(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c(1, 7),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  )

ggplot(
  temp_df,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = mean_tmax,
    group = id
  )
) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.15, color = "blue") +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature in January and July",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Maximum Temperature (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 9),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )
```


Summary of the plots:
July has much higher average maximum temperatures (mostly around 25–30°C) than January (mostly around −5–5°C). There is variation among stations in both months, shown by the many overlapping lines. January temperatures appear more variable than July temperatures. There is no obvious long-term increasing or decreasing trend in either panel. Temperatures fluctuate from year to year.

Potential outliers: A few stations show unusually low values. In July, some observations fall well below the main cluster, including one in the late 1980s. In January, a few observations fall below −10°C.
